title: Carnegie Hall in 1956 and the college president
summary: Playing Carnegie Hall, press attention, the Presbyterian president, Jack Crystal's announcement, and Donny Andre's booking.

blocks.x: The High Street Five from Wesleyan. There are a handful of them but the Catatonic Five was highly rated. The fact that we played at Carnegie Hall in ’56, and toured Europe that same year, so I thought it actually reflected very favorably on the college. Here’s this little tiny college that’s got the best Dixieland — one of the best Dixieland bands in the country, and was getting a lot of press. And I think we were proud of that and frankly, I’m not sure Sandy McEwen was very proud, you know Sandy who didn’t allow no jazz on Sunday—
Oh you can’t just gloss over that you have to tell me about that.

Well I’ll let Dick Sherman tell you about that, that’s his story. But the president was a Presbyterian minister and he wasn’t much of a jazz fan. But I think most people thought it was great. I mean gee, here’s a big placard, there’s a midnight jam session at Carnegie Hall on November 24 and it’s Hamilton College. And who announced this but Jack Crystal, Billy Crystal’s dad. And so I think it was good for the college and I think people recognized that.
And how did that gig come about?
Donny Andre will have to tell you that. Don was just great about getting these various gigs for us including the one to Europe which was wonderful.
